key_insight: A chemically active viscous drop near a rigid wall swims faster when it stays closer to the wall, and its speed is only weakly affected by the balance between Marangoni and diffusiophoretic surface flows at moderate Peclet number.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical rule for predicting and controlling active droplet motion in confined microfluidic and chemical-transport settings, and it supports simpler active-particle models for design studies.
method: Model steady translation of a chemically active viscous drop parallel to a rigid wall.
Include coupled solute advection-diffusion, interfacial Marangoni stresses, and diffusiophoretic flows.
Compare the full droplet model against the isotropic active-particle approximation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical comparison showing that, under the same confining force, lower-viscosity drops sit closer to the wall and swim faster, with speed depending only weakly on mobility ratio at moderate Pe.
watch_item: The simplified active-particle picture may miss important chemo-hydrodynamic wall effects when viscosity contrast or confinement strongly alters the flow and concentration field.
paper_title: Steady translation of a chemically active viscous drop along a rigid wall
